title: A cloud credential or private key file is exposed
summary: A file that holds cloud credentials or a private key is being served to anyone. An outsider who reads an AWS, Google Cloud, Docker or s3cmd credential file, or an SSH or TLS private key, can sign in to the account or service it belongs to with no guessing, which is how several large breaches began. This check only reports the file when its body actually carries a credential marker, so a plain not-found page is never a finding.

confirm.control: A path that cannot exist, so the site's not found answer is known and a credential file is told apart from a soft 404 or a catch-all page.
confirm.differential: status == 200 and (body_contains("aws_access_key_id") or body_contains("aws_secret_access_key") or (body_contains("\"private_key\"") and body_contains("\"client_email\"")) or (body_contains("\"auths\"") and body_contains("\"auth\"")) or (body_contains("access_key") and body_contains("secret_key")) or body_contains("PRIVATE KEY-----")) and body_differs(control)

reproduce: curl -sk 'https://host/.aws/credentials' (and the other candidate paths this check tried) and read the body.  An AWS file shows aws_access_key_id and aws_secret_access_key; a Google service account shows "private_key" and "client_email"; a Docker config shows "auths" with an "auth" token; an s3cmd or boto file shows access_key and secret_key; an SSH or TLS key shows a PRIVATE KEY----- block.  If any returns the secret, treat it as live and rotate it.
remediate: Remove the file from the web root and from anything the server will serve, then rotate every credential it exposed, since it must be assumed to have been read.  Serve application code from a directory that does not include dotfiles or deployment artifacts, and add a rule that denies requests for credential and key files.  Keep secrets in a secret manager or environment, never in a file under the document root.
